body.“This case demonstrates the importance of preserving evidence, even when decades have passed,” said the Salt Lake county sheriff, Rosie Rivera, on Tuesday. “We have the ability to take a look at these cases again and again.”Between 1974 and 1978, Bundy went on a violent rampage, sexually assaulting and killing at least 30 women across the American west and Florida.“The voices and cherished memories of Melissa Ann Smith and Laura Ann Aime and others involved in these cases ring louder than the hate and sedition of the one that took their lives,” said Mike Reynolds, a sergeant with the Utah county sheriff’s office, on Tuesday. “With every case closure may we stomp the memory of Ted Bundy out.”Explore more on these topicsUtahUS crimenewsShareReuse this content

title: Body of missing California hiker covered in snow retrieved on Mount Whitney | California | The Guardian
description: Hazardous storm conditions delayed recovery efforts on mountain that has proved to be a perilous hiking spot
Author: Uwa Ede-Osifo
Headline: Hazardous storm conditions delayed recovery efforts on mountain that has proved to be a perilous hiking spot
Content: Mount Whitney is the highest mountain in the contiguous US.Photograph: AaronP/Bauer-Griffin/GC ImagesView image in fullscreenMount Whitney is the highest mountain in the contiguous US.Photograph: AaronP/Bauer-Griffin/GC ImagesCaliforniaBody of missing California hiker covered in snow retrieved on Mount WhitneyHazardous storm conditions delayed recovery efforts on mountain that has proved to be a perilous hiking spotUwa Ede-OsifoTue 27 Oct 2026 19.39 EDTLast modified on Tue 27 Oct 2026 21.37 EDTSharePrefer the Guardian on GoogleThe body of a missingCaliforniahiker, blanketed in a layer of snow, was recovered on Mount Whitney on Sunday after a blustery storm delayed retrieval operations for five days.The Inyo county sheriff’s office extended its condolences to the loved ones and family of the hiker, who has not been publicly identified, in a Monday statement.On 19 October, a motel in Lone Pine, a town in California’s Sierra Nevada region, contacted the sheriff’s office about a guest who failed to check out. The man had brought up plans to hike in the area.A vehicle belonging to the climber was found the next day at the base of Mount Whitney. The California highway patrol deployed a helicopter, which found the deceased man on the Mountaineer’s Route, a steep nine mile path leading to the mountain’s peak.A storm system which brought hazardous weather conditions hindered authorities from securing the man’s body. A county search and rescue team was deployed on Sunday and the individual was hoisted off the mountain via helicopter from an elevation of about 13,600 ft.Mount Whitney, the tallest mountain in the contiguous United States, has proven to be a perilous hiking site in recent years.In October, 52-year-old Fresno builder Kalem Peter Kazariandiedwhile hiking.Last December, Joseph Brambila, a 21-year-old solo hiker celebrating his birthday wasmissing for weeksbefore he was found dead.Explore more on these topicsCaliforniaWest CoastMountainsnewsShareReuse this content

title: Four takeaways from Anthropic’s potentially record-breaking stock market filing | Anthropic | The Guardian
description: The AI company’s first public financial disclosures reveal explosive growth, huge costs and risks ranging from cyber-attacks to the limits of safeguards
Author: Johana Bhuiyan
Headline: The AI company’s first public financial disclosures reveal explosive growth, huge costs and risks ranging from cyber-attacks to the limits of safeguards
Content: The 92-page document released on Monday talks about Anthropic’s explosive growth and the risks AI has brought to the business.Photograph: Kim Kyung-Hoon/ReutersView image in fullscreenThe 92-page document released on Monday talks about Anthropic’s explosive growth and the risks AI has brought to the business.Photograph: Kim Kyung-Hoon/ReutersAnthropicExplainerFour takeaways from Anthropic’s potentially record-breaking stock market filingThe AI company’s first public financial disclosures reveal explosive growth, huge costs and risks ranging from cyber-attacks to the limits of safeguardsJohana BhuiyanTue 27 Oct 2026 01.00 EDTLast modified on Tue 27 Oct 2026 11.27 EDTSharePrefer the Guardian on GoogleAnthropichas filedto go public on the US stock market, revealing for the first time the AI research lab’s financials and all the risks – more than 90 pages of them – that might negatively affect its business.The company’s investor prospectus, released on Monday, veers from hyperbolic predictions about AI’s “incredible potential” to existential risks of the technology to the reality of its current business: explosive but incredibly expensive growth. The filing to US financial regulators, known as an S-1, provides the public’s first look at an audited version of Anthropic’s finances.Here are some of the key takeaways from Anthropic’s lengthy S-1.Anthropic reveals rapid revenue gains and larger losses in stock market filingRead more1.Explosive and expensive growthHere’s what you need to know: Anthropic is making a lot of money. It’s also losing a lot of it. The five-year-old firm has been valued between $1.5 and $2tn by some investors but did not list a target valuation in its S-1. Founded in 2021, the company has seen explosive growth every year of its existence.Anthropic brought in $16.3bn in revenue and lost $80bn in just the first half of 2026, though much of that was due to a $72.4bn one-off charge. In 2025, the company brought in $4.585bn and lost roughly $33.9bn, per the filing.Column chart showing quarterly filings from Anthropic from Q1 2025 to Q2 2026. While revenues are increasing quarter over quarter, net losses are increasing at a faster rate.Securing computing power accounts for the vast majority of Anthropic’s costs. The company spent nearly $9bn on AI infrastructure in the first half of this year, up from $2.3bn in the same period last year.Anthropic, unlike OpenAI, has made it clear that its customers are largely other businesses. “Frontier AI is most valuable in real-world settings, as deployment across enterprises is where economic impact is greatest,” the company executives wrote in the filing.The company said its top five customers account for 25% of its business – which makes it risky business.2.‘A country of geniuses in a datacenter’Anthropic says there is considerable potential for AI to reach levels of intelligence that would be akin to what its executives called “‘a country of geniuses in a datacenter’ – millions of virtual agents with the ability to revolutionize every area of human endeavor: software, physics, math, biology, medicine, finance, economics, commerce, robotics, military and intelligence capabilities”. Noticeably, the company mentioned military capabilities despite being embroiled in a standoff with the Trump administration over its refusal to limit restrictions on the way the Department of Defense could use Claude.The company highlighted four specific categories of opportunity at the start of the filing: Acceleration of progress in biology and medicine; economic growth; spreading said growth globally; and streamlining government services (such as social services and medical programming).The company said it was already working with several pharmaceutical and biotechnology companies and improved the process for clinical trials, which is “cutting the time it takes to write clinical trial reports from months to minutes”.The company’s executives claim they have also made biological discoveries with Claude, including a “molecular machine” that has the “potential to be developed into a novel biotechnology tool”. One purported use case: gene editing.3.AI ‘safeguards are incomplete’The company discusses risks in two contexts: the dangers that AI itself poses to society and human beings, and the ways Anthropic’s business could go awry.Risks that AI poses were broken down into four main categories: misuse by bad actors, loss of control, authoritarian abuse and economic disruption. While Anthropic put a great deal of emphasis on the guardrails it has implemented to block attempts to misuse its models, it also includes one big caveat later in the filing: those safeguards may not work.Anthropic’s most capable models are capable of providing “meaningful assistance to malicious actors seeking to develop chemical, biological, or other dangerous weapons”, the company’s executives wrote in the filing.The company deploys technical safeguards, “but such safeguards are incomplete, may be outdated in light of evolving threat models, have been and may in the future again be circumvented, or may fail to operate as intended”.Already, Anthropic has detected what it believes is the first documented case of a large-scale cyber-attack with little human intervention. The company believes a Chinese state-sponsored hacking group manipulated a Claude code tool “into attempting infiltration into roughly 30 global targets, including large technology companies, financial institutions, chemical manufacturing companies, and government agencies”, per the prospectus.The company said it recognized AI may be used by authoritarian governments to “deepen repression” and develop “high-tech surveillance states”. Anthropic presented less of a defense or potential safeguard against those uses and instead said it was committed to working with “free societies to provide a counterweight to authoritarian abuse and to promote freedom and democracy”. The firm seems to suggest that its work with what it describes with scant details as “free societies” will cancel out in some way the AI-enabled repression of authoritarian regimes.The company had a falling out with the Trump administration after the firm said it would not change its restrictions to allow its models to be used to build domestic surveillance or autonomous lethal weapons.4.92 pages of financial riskAnthropic goes into detail in laying out 92 pages of risks to its business. Investors are making sense of a type of company that is fairly new to the public market in a highly competitive space with everything to lose.The company acknowledges that much of its success is tied to its top executives and whether they stay at the firm, being able to edge out its main competitors Google and OpenAI, navigating the tumultuous regulatory landscape around AI and datacenters and surviving any public relations fallout over its AI models being used to do things they are not supposed to do, likecreate bioweapons.The company’s focus on enterprise customers means that if any of its top buyers leave, the company could take a huge hit.Anthropic’s structure as a public benefit corporation – which is a designation for a for-profit company that balances financial interests with achieving a stated social good – may make it harder to achieve its short – or medium-term financial goals, the company said. The firm is obliged to report on its progress in meeting its public benefit goals in the same way it has to report its financials.There’s also all the risk related to any AI-enabled catastrophic event – the sort of doomsday scenario Anthropic employees have been warning about. Anthropic’s CEO, Dario Amodei, has called for a pause on AI development to ensure firms are developing it responsibly to avoid any such catastrophe. In addition to the public harm and potential fallout over a scenario where Claude went rogue, Anthropic said they worry they will be subject to a great deal of liability, especially considering insurance options for AI are still evolving.“We may be unable to obtain coverage for certain AI-related liabilities on commercially reasonable terms, or at all, leaving us exposed to potentially significant uninsured losses,” the filing reads.The bedrock of Anthropic’s AI infrastructure is concentrated in the US, making it extremely vulnerable to regulatory changes, power grid constraints, natural disasters and opposition to AI or datacenters. The filing specifically calls out datacenter moratoriums that have been passed or are being considered as among the big issues they are concerned about.“We are expanding our data center capacity internationally as part of our efforts to diversify our infrastructure footprint and reduce concentration risks,” the filing reads.The company, which says a big part of its value proposition is its talent, also said it worries about US immigration policies affecting its ability to recruit and retain highly qualified employees. The Trump administration has targeted H-1B visas, a tool tech firms have come to rely on to attract and hire from the global pool of tech and engineering talent.Explore more on these topicsAnthropicAI (artificial intelligence)Internet IPOsTechnology sectorChatbotskey takeawaysShareReuse this content

title: Chinese markets lose trillions as race for AI supremacy with US takes its toll | China | The Guardian
description: Lack of profits and the threat posed by western countries are raising concern about the sustainability of Beijing’s AI boom
Author: Amy Hawkins
Headline: Lack of profits and the threat posed by western countries are raising concern about the sustainability of Beijing’s AI boom
Content: Beijing has doubled down on robotics – also known as embodied AI – as the key to rolling out the technology across society.Photograph: China News Service/Getty ImagesView image in fullscreenBeijing has doubled down on robotics – also known as embodied AI – as the key to rolling out the technology across society.Photograph: China News Service/Getty ImagesChinaChinese markets lose trillions as race for AI supremacy with US takes its tollLack of profits and the threat posed by western countries are raising concern about the sustainability of Beijing’s AI boomAmy Hawkinsin BeijingTue 27 Oct 2026 00.42 EDTLast modified on Tue 27 Oct 2026 10.09 EDTSharePrefer the Guardian on GoogleTrillions of dollars have been wiped from China’s stock markets in recent months amid increasing anxiety about the future of artificial intelligence, as Beijing races against the United States for dominance in the sector.The STAR 50 Index, which tracks technology and innovation companies on the Shanghai stock exchange, has plunged 40% since June. Other indexes of major companies dropped by about 20% over the same time period.The precipitous drop has wiped out $2.4tn from the Chinese stock market since May, according to Bloomberg.AI stocks account for over 40% of the stock market value in China and Hong Kong, according to Goldman Sachs, meaning that any dent in value will send shockwaves across the whole domestic market.3:48Why the US government is banning Chinese robots – video explainerUS bans use of China’s DeepSeek AI tools by government agenciesRead moreThe fall suggests that despite the government’s best efforts to boost China’s technology industries, particularly those which harness the power of AI, the domestic economy does not have the power to sustain a booming market.The Chinese government has invested heavily into AI, including a 60bn yuan state-backed AI investment fund which started pumping money into domestic developers this month. But Chinese consumers have proved stubbornly reluctant to part with their cash in many parts of the economy – including technology – meaning that many tech companies struggle to turn a profit.The lack of profits is one of several reasons for the sell-off. Another is the threat of western countries, especially the US, extending bans on Chinese technology.“This year, the profit margin is not as good as expected. And the US is raising rates. And China’s domestic demand is so weak,” said Dan Wang, the China director for the Eurasia Group. She said that there was a “general anxiety” among technology companies about whether or not the state-backed model would work in the face of weak consumer demand.The US hasbanned humanoid robots from China, citing national security risks, and is thought to beconsidering a banon Chinese components in data centres. China is heavily reliant on exports and restrictions in the US hurt its domestic companies, which struggle to sell enough products at home.As China races with the US to pull ahead in AI, Beijing has doubled down onrobotics– also known as embodied AI – as the key to rolling out the technology across society. Robotics is also seen as the answer to China’s demographic problems, such as the ageing population and the shrinking workforce.But the demand for robotics is being driven by government agencies and research institutions, rather than everyday consumers, for whom the products are still too expensive and not yet practical for home use. Humanoid robotics and robotic dogs have been popular in the entertainment industry but are yet to be useful in home settings.Shares in Unitree, China’s leading robot-maker, have halved since they started trading in August.“It doesn’t look like embodied intelligence could turn into profits in the in the mass market,” said Wang. Thin profit margins, rising rates in the US, and weak domestic demand were all contributing to a “general anxiety” among technology companies, she said.View image in fullscreenHumanoid robotics and robotic dogs have been popular in the entertainment industry but are yet to be useful in home settings.Photograph: Costfoto/NurPhoto/ShutterstockChina’s government wants local investors to invest their money domestically. China has in recent months restricted overseas investment, with more regulations taking effect from 1 December, but these moves have not led to greater investment in the Chinese markets.Wang added that there was still optimism in other technology sectors, such as AI research and satellites, the latter because their links to the military indicates long term state support for the sector. And globally the AI boom is expected to last for at least another year.On Monday, US AI company Anthropic, which makes the chatbot Claude,filed paperwork ahead of a planned IPOthat could be the biggest stock market debuts of all time. The company is expected to bring in as much as $100bn.China has no such blockbuster IPOs on the horizon. And despite pressure on policymakers to introduce stimulus measures to boost investment, none are expected to be announced during a politically sensitive period in China.This week thetop officials in the Chinese Communist party are gathering for the fifth plenum, an important meeting that will lay the groundwork for next year’s 21st Party Congress. The Congress is expected to anoint Xi Jinping, China’s leader, for a fourth term. There is no appetite for risky or potentially destabilising policy measures before then, even if there is a chance they could boost the economy.Any stimulus measure would be “high risk”, Wang said. “What if it doesn’t work out? Then whoever came up with that policy, that guy would be held accountable”.Explore more on these topicsChinaAI (artificial intelligence)Stock marketsAsia PacificnewsShareReuse this content

title: The survival of American democracy depends on taxing billionaires | US taxation | The Guardian
description: It is essential not just to fund the public goods the nation needs, it is indispensable to restore a sense of fairness
Author: Eduardo Porter
Headline: It is essential not just to fund the public goods the nation needs, it is indispensable to restore a sense of fairness
Content: Supporters listen to Senator Bernie Sanders during a campaign rally in support of California Proposition 40, known as the billionaire tax, in Los Angeles, on 5 October 2026.Photograph: Jae C Hong/APView image in fullscreenSupporters listen to Senator Bernie Sanders during a campaign rally in support of California Proposition 40, known as the billionaire tax, in Los Angeles, on 5 October 2026.Photograph: Jae C Hong/APUS taxationAnalysisThe survival of American democracy depends on taxing billionairesEduardo PorterIt is essential not just to fund the public goods the nation needs, it is indispensable to restore a sense of fairnessTue 27 Oct 2026 07.00 EDTLast modified on Tue 27 Oct 2026 17.38 EDTShareMoney doesn’t buy happiness, we’re told. Even some economists agree. The Nobel prize-winning economists Daniel Kahneman and Angus Deaton onceproposed thatrising income increased people’s emotional wellbeing only up to a ceiling of about $115,000 in today’s money.They probably hadn’t met many billionaires. The ultra-rich may not pursue happiness in the joyful sense of the word. But they will try every trick in the book to hang on to their stash and woe betide the tax authority that tries to lay a finger on their treasure.And this poses one of the most intractable challenges not only to the solvency of the American state, but to the survival of American democracy.From the technological Olympus ofSilicon Valleyto the urbancanyons of Wall Street, a narrow club of vastly wealthy plutocrats sits on a ballooning share of the nation’s resources. One per cent of Americans at the apex of the economy arehoarding over 31%of the nation’s total wealth, acool $55tnin net worth.Getting them to share with the rest of society, to fund redistribution or pay for public goods, is proving pretty much impossible. Their ability to move resources around, hide profit across jurisdictions, and minimize income to hoard wealth until they die appears to put them beyond the reach of taxation.One recent research paperfound that the country’s richest 384 oligarchs paid only 24% of their economic income in 2025, compared with 30% for the average taxpayer. And not all of them are getting top-notch tax advice.Reporting by ProPublicarevealed that some of the richest Americans – like Elon Musk, Jeff Bezos, Warren Buffett and Michael Bloomberg – live largely tax free.California is experimenting with a budgetary Hail Mary pass: In November,Californians will be called to voteon Proposition 40, a one-time 5% tax on the wealth of billionaires residing in the state on 1 January of this year. If the plutocracy’s income is off limits, the thinking goes, best to target its gargantuan assets.California’s gambit is “the first-ever tax on billionaire wealth enacted anywhere in the world” – according toan open letterendorsing the move by six Nobel prize-winning economists on the left side of the political spectrum. “It will kickstart a movement to tax ultra-high-net-worth individuals in other states – and eventually at the federal level and in other countries,” they raved. The vote “may well come to be seen as a turning point in the battle between democracy and oligarchy”.Moreover, Prop 40 couldraise real money. As of early October,260 billionaires lived in the state, according to the Forbes billionaires’ list, amassing nearly $2.5tn in wealth. Based on these numbers, the 5% tax would raise some $110bn, much of which would go to replace Medicaid funding nixed in Trump’s One Big Beautiful Bill Act last year.Still, the move is proving controversial even among left-leaning economists and politicians. Governor Gavin Newsom, who is virtually certain to run for the Democratic nomination ahead of the 2028 presidential election, is opposed. So is Xavier Becerra, the Democrat running to succeed him as governor. They fear that such a move will spark a flight of the oligarchs to lower-tax jurisdictions.View image in fullscreenPeople attend a rally against Proposition 40 at the Iron Workers Apprenticeship Training Center on 5 October 2026 in La Palma, California.Photograph: Eric Thayer/Los Angeles Times/Getty ImagesThe Nobelists note that the California’s proposed billionaire tax was sneaked in to prevent billionaires from fleeing to avoid it: “Some affected taxpayers may have tried to leave between the time they learned about the proposed ballot initiative – in late November 2025 – and January 1st of 2026,” they wrote. “But the window was so short that it is unlikely any significant number of billionaires successfully cut ties with the Golden State in such a short period of time.”In fact, between January and October the number of billionaires living in California grew by 20. Elon Musk may believe that welfare recipients are the “parasite class” and empathy is “the fundamental weakness of western civilization”. But perhaps California’s billionaires feel enough empathy for less fortunate humans to part with a paltry $110bn, especially since their wealth has grown by a cool $400bn so far this year.Not all billionaires move to avoid taxes. Trump’s 2017 Tax Cuts and Jobs Act, which capped the state and local tax deduction, was expected to prompt the rich to flee high-tax blue states in droves, as they could no longer deduct their state and local tax payments on their federal tax returns. But a study by a Cornell sociologist and an economist at the treasury departmentfound almost no impacton the migration rates of the affluent, at least in the first year following the change.Indeed, the rich in New York City are hit by a top city income tax rate of 3.9% on top of a 10.9% state tax, compared with zero in Miami. Still, there are 154 billionaires in New York state, according toa report by Oxfam. Nine of the 10 richest live in the city. The only state with more billionaires than New York is, wait, high-tax California.Still, Newsom and Becerra have a point. California’s richest billionaires have gone feral over Prop 40. Google’s Sergey Brin has helped coordinate about $200m tooppose itand promote two countervailing propositions,41 and 42that, if passed, would emasculate the tax. One would bar retroactive taxes – putting wealth accumulated in the past off limits – and forbid new taxes on financial assets or other personal property.The opposition is gaining traction.A poll in Septemberfound that Prop 40 falls just short of majority approval. Just in case, the fast money has tried to flee the state, to make it out before deadline. In the run-up to Christmas of 2025 Brin and the Google co-founder Larry Page moved many of their business interestsout of California. They also bought homes out of state. Travis Kalanick, former CEO of Uber, followed Musk to Texas. Paypal and Palantir mogul Peter Thiel moved his residence to Miami last year.While some of the more optimistic analyses assume that avoidance tactics by California billionaires will reduce the taxable pot of wealth by only about 10%, others are less sanguine. Even if it passes, the tax will be taken to court, including on grounds that retroactive taxation violates due process, and may not survive litigation. Some assets – real estate, notably – will not be taxed. Foreign billionaires may wiggle out under double taxation treaties. And more billionaires will leave, assuming that though it was billed as a one-time affair, the new tax will become permanent. This will hit future income tax revenues.Altogether, economists from Stanford Universityconcluded thatthe new tax would raise only around $30bn, while the flow of lost income tax revenue would cost state coffers nearly $39bn, in net present value. The estimate fits with results from studies of attempts to avoid wealth taxesin Swiss cantons. It also checks with behavioral responses of the rich to other forms of taxation. For instance, Enrico Moretti, an economist at the University of California Berkeley, and Daniel Wilson of the Federal Reserve Bank of San Francisco, found the location of the very rich is highly sensitive toestate taxes.These should be the most American taxes of them all, a good fit for a democratic nation that conceives itself as a meritocracy; a tool to prevent the emergence of a hereditary aristocracy passing economic and political power down the generations. Still, the rich don’t much care for them.skip past newsletter promotionFree newsletter |Weekly, for twelve weeksSign up toHow We WinBernie Sanders, Robert Reich, Stacey Abrams, Mehdi Hasan, Paul Krugman and other bold thinkers on how to defeat Trumpism and build a better future. From our opinion desk.Enter your emailSign upafter newsletter promotionIn 2001, George W Bush did what Republican presidents do: he cut taxes. But his Economic Growth Tax Relief and Reconciliation Act included an annoying twist: it eliminated the credit offered by the federal government to offset the estate tax burden imposed by states on the ultra-wealthy. All of a sudden, billionaires’ estate tax liability became dependent on which state they lived in. Dying as a resident of New York, Pennsylvania and Connecticut, which had estate taxes, abruptly become way more costly than dying in a state with none, like Texas, Florida … or California.By 2010, over a fifth of billionaires in the Forbes 400 list who originally lived in a state that levied an estate tax state had moved to a non-estate tax state, while only about 1% had made a move in the opposite direction. Moretti and Wilson estimated that by 2017 states with estate taxes had lost 23 of 72 Forbes 400 billionaires who lived there in 2001. Altogether, Forbes 400 wealth subject to state estate taxes fell from some $203bn in 2001 to about $122bn 16 years later.States with estate taxes didn’t just lose the income tax revenue of their departing billionaires. Extra losses not considered in Moretti and Wilson’s analysis include the effect of plutocrats relocating their businesses. Moreover, estate taxes could well deter other billionaires from moving into the state, or encourage those who remained to try more aggressive tax avoidance strategies than usual.In light of the difficulties in taxing billionaires andeven the lesser rich, there is an argument out there that a less progressive, flatter tax structure could do better at raising money. European countries fund a large share of their generous welfare programs with value added taxes on consumption, which are more difficult to avoid but place a heavier burden on lower-income people who consume a larger share of their paychecks.And yet the idea of letting plutocracy off the hook seems unacceptable. Brin has said Prop 40 reminds him of the Soviet Union, which he fled with his parents in 1979. Apparently he prefers a social arrangement more like the one that prevailed in the Tsarist Russia in which a narrow few amass vast riches unencumbered by a responsibility to contribute to societal wellbeing. That’s the America we all live in now.If American democracy is to survive this moment, it must figure out a way for billionaires to contribute more. It is essential not just to fund the public goods the nation needs to function. It’s indispensable to restore a sense of fairness to the American experiment. Democracy cannot endure without it.Let’s see what happens next month in California. But the hard truth for blue states eager to raise more revenue to fund the social safety net and pay for public goods is that they are not up to the task, given competition with Republican-run states where taxes are anathema. As Moretti points out, the tax gap between red states and blue states has become enormous. California’s top marginal rate is 13.5%. Florida’s is zero. The temptation for the next Tsarist plutocrat to move from the first to the second is not insignificant.Indeed, Moretti and Wilson have anotherresearch paperthat looks at what top scientists and engineers do when states raise income taxes. “People do leave,” Moretti told me. “These are not billionaires, but only highly paid workers.”The good news is that while there are many ways in which California’s attempt at taking a nibble out of billionaires’ wealth may fail, it is not technically impossible to tax the oligarchy. There arevarious optionsavailable. Federal estate tax rules could be cleansed of the myriad loopholes that allow dynastic wealth to accumulate, such as those allowing unrealized capital gains to accrue forever tax free and bequeathed to heirs with the gains reset to zero. Taxes on capital income could be raised to restore fairness between taxation on capital and labor.Economists Erick Zwick of the University of Chicago and Owen Zidar of Princetonpropose thatrestoring the tax schedule to where it was in the Clinton administration 30 years ago would raise $5tn over a decade and do wonders for America’s public finances. The main challenge to that is political: it requires an overhaul of a political equilibrium that over the last 50 years has largely revolved around cutting taxes.But restoring fairness and efficacy to the American state is in the end not a task for the states. Altogether, the government collects almost 3% of GDP less in taxes than it did at the turn of the century. Over 2% of that decline was about federal revenues. The average central government in the Organization for Economic Cooperation and Development today raises twice as much in taxes, as a share of GDP, as the US federal government.Fixing this is, of course, a political problem, one that will remain intractable as long as half of the political spectrum believes its only job on this Earth is to cut taxes. But it would be helpful for the fleet-footed billionaires to give some thought to the social contract in which they want to live; whether they are interested in broad-based prosperity or, rather, they are happy to slink into their castle, raise the drawbridge, and hope societal upheaval does not interrupt dinner.Explore more on these topicsUS taxationUS midterm elections 2026US economyUS income inequalityCaliforniaUS politicsanalysisShareReuse this content

title: Sliding Colts trade All-Pro guard Quenton Nelson to Seahawks for draft picks | NFL | The Guardian
description: Indianapolis, who have lost three straight and fired their general manager last week, will receive a pair of draft picks in exchange for the eight-time Pro Bowler
Author: Guardian staff reporter
Headline: Indianapolis, who have lost three straight and fired their general manager last week, will receive a pair of draft picks in exchange for the eight-time Pro Bowler
Content: Quenton Nelson will join the Seahawks after eight full seasons with the Colts.Photograph: Adam Bettcher/APView image in fullscreenQuenton Nelson will join the Seahawks after eight full seasons with the Colts.Photograph: Adam Bettcher/APNFLSliding Colts trade All-Pro guard Quenton Nelson to Seahawks for draft picks30-year-old is an eight-time Pro Bowl selectionIndianapolis fired GM Ballard last week amid skidAssociated PressTue 27 Oct 2026 15.18 EDTLast modified on Tue 27 Oct 2026 15.25 EDTSharePrefer the Guardian on GoogleTheIndianapolis Coltshave traded All-Pro guard Quenton Nelson to the Seattle Seahawks, a person with knowledge of the deal told the Associated Press on Tuesday.The person requested anonymity because the deal had not been announced by either team and said the Colts would receive a third-round draft pick and a fifth-round pick in return for the eight-time Pro Bowler.Nelson can become a free agent in March, but he had not said much about his future plans because he was focused on finishing this season strong.Creaking, smug … and a contender? Aaron Rodgers may yet get his Super Bowl farewellRead moreIt’s the second major move in two weeks for Indianapolis (2-5), who have lost three straight and 12 of their past 14 overall. The Colts fired general manager Chris Ballard last week after a loss to the previously winless Tennessee Titans at home. Assistant general manager Ed Dodds has replaced Ballard for now.Nelson was the No 6 overall pick in 2018 and joined linebacker Darius Leonard on the All-Pro team, making the duo the first rookie teammates to earn All-Pro honors since the Chicago Bears’ Gale Sayers and Dick Butkus in 1965. Nelson was an All-Pro from 2018 to 2020.The Colts visit Jacksonville (4-2) on Sunday while the Seahawks (4-3) host Chicago (5-2) on Monday night.Explore more on these topicsNFLIndianapolis ColtsSeattle SeahawksUS sportsnewsShareReuse this content

title: Fantastic Fleetwood seal shootout success in Carabao Cup shock against Arsenal | Carabao Cup | The Guardian
description: Conor Haughey scored the winning penalty in Fleetwood’s 5-3 shootout win against 10-man Arsenal, after the Carabao Cup fourth round tie finished 1-1
Author: Will Unwin
Headline: Conor Haughey scored the winning penalty in Fleetwood’s 5-3 shootout win against 10-man Arsenal, after the Carabao Cup fourth round tie finished 1-1
Content: Rhys Bennett leads the celebrations after Fleetwood’s dramatic shootout win.Photograph: Jon Super/ReutersView image in fullscreenRhys Bennett leads the celebrations after Fleetwood’s dramatic shootout win.Photograph: Jon Super/ReutersCarabao CupFantastic Fleetwood seal shootout success in Carabao Cup shock against ArsenalWill Unwinat Highbury StadiumTue 27 Oct 2026 18.26 EDTLast modified on Tue 27 Oct 2026 19.57 EDTSharePrefer the Guardian on GoogleIt is more than 20 years since Arsenal played at Highbury but their trip to League Two Fleetwood – and a stadium of the same name – did not bring back fond memories as they were dumped out of theCarabao Cupon penalties. It was the team with red shirts and white sleeves that triumphed, but on this occasion it caused one of the greatest upsets in English football history.Aaron Loupalo-Bi and Viktor Gyökeres exchanged goals in normal time butArsenalwere unable to find a winner, despite being the dominant force, as Fleetwood battled to the end. The home manager, Matt Lawlor, was almost in tears, unable to cope after the tension was released when Conor Haughey smashed the ball into the top corner to settle the shootout.Fleetwood Town stun Arsenal on penalties: Carabao Cup fourth round – liveRead moreThat came after Jay Lynch had saved from Bruno Guimarães, a former warehouse worker stopping the Brazilian international. It is the storylines everyone wants but so rarely gets in the sanitised modern football world.Fleetwood were aiming to earn £400,000 from the night but got something priceless in the end. Everyone in attendance will never forget they saw the fourth-tier side knock out thePremier League champions. Of course they had to ride their luck and were helped by Max Dowman’s debatable sending off but football is rarely about logic, it is one of emotion. This is once in a lifetime for the Cod Army, for anyone at their level, and they enjoyed it.A year ago Lawlor was not even a football manager, he never played professionally and started his coaching career with the Manchester United Foundation. Lynch had spent much of his early career in non-league, only dreaming of playing a team who narrowlylost the Champions League finalin the spring.Everyone was expecting a routine victory, even with Mikel Arteta giving youngsters the chance to impress. If Arteta wanted to test his youngsters then Marli Salmon’s naivety was shown up by Loupalo-Bi, on loan from Fulham.He has been learning his trade in the fourth tier this season and put into practice the skill of using his body against a defender, spinning and holding off the 17-year-old before slotting under Illan Meslier to bring lift-off for the second time of the night.View image in fullscreenAaron Loupalo-Bi fires Fleetwood into a first-half lead.Photograph: Jon Super/ReutersBy that point the game had already had a six-minute delay due to a drone being flown above the pitch. The referee Michael Salisbury had to take the players to the sidelines while the police searched for the culprit outside the ground. It was an unordinary start to what became an extraordinary night on the Fylde Coast. It had started with a plethora of pyrotechnics that created a red haze across the pitch and, frankly, it never dissipated, literally or metaphorically.The first half was one of toil for Arsenal, unable to create anything meaningful, constantly being thwarted by the disciplined defence, well organised by Lawlor and his staff. The Gunners were pedestrian against a team happy to watch them go through the motions. Kai Havertz missed the best chance to equalise before the break but his header was wayward, summing up a difficult match for him.View image in fullscreenBruno Guimarães’ penalty is saved by the Fleetwood goalkeeper Jay Lynch.Photograph: Nick Potts/PAAfter the break it was different as Martin Ødegaard came on to become the quarterback for Arsenal, creating the rhythm they had sorely lacked. He brought cohesion and intensity, getting them back into the game.skip past newsletter promotionFree newsletter |Every weekdaySign up toFootball DailyKick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of footballEnter your emailSign upafter newsletter promotionIt was Gyökeres who bundled home the equaliser and few would have doubted Arsenal going on to win the match but Fleetwood held firm.The home side had been direct from the start, accepting their limitations and knowing the conditions would help them. Swirling wind helped hold the ball up in the sky and confused defenders not used to the gales by the sea.Fleetwood’s robust play irritated Arsenal and Dowman was wound up, getting himself sent off for reacting to enforcer-in-chief Harrison Neal. He was the second Gunners teenager to learn a valuable lesson of life outside the top flight after Salmon was exposed for the goal.It may have been harsh but it was needlessly petulant from Dowman on an already challenging night for his side. Mikel Arteta had a word with him on the way off. What did Arteta say? “Something that we discussed already before the match.”Arsenal had two late chances through Ben White and Gyökeres to settle it before the need for spot-kicks, but Lynch produced two fantastic saves as the clock went past 90 minutes to ensure it went to a fittingly dramatic finale, where he could be the hero again on a great night for football and the town of Fleetwood.Explore more on these topicsCarabao CupFleetwood TownArsenalmatch reportsShareReuse this content

title: An unmanageable club? Carrick the latest to suffer in Manchester United’s faded grandeur | Manchester United | The Guardian
description: Only Matt Busby and Alex Ferguson have truly succeeded in the Old Trafford hot seat with each casting uneasy shadows
Author: John Brewin
Headline: Only Matt Busby and Alex Ferguson have truly succeeded in the Old Trafford hot seat with each casting uneasy shadows
Content: Manchester United managers past and present: Matt Busby (top left), Frank O'Farrell (bottom left), Tommy Docherty (third left), Michael Carrick (centre), David Moyes (third right), Erik ten Hag (bottom right) and Alex Ferguson.Composite: Guardian Pictures; Popperfoto/Getty Images; PA; Tom Jenkins/The Guardian; Action Images; Shutterstock; ReutersView image in fullscreenManchester United managers past and present: Matt Busby (top left), Frank O'Farrell (bottom left), Tommy Docherty (third left), Michael Carrick (centre), David Moyes (third right), Erik ten Hag (bottom right) and Alex Ferguson.Composite: Guardian Pictures; Popperfoto/Getty Images; PA; Tom Jenkins/The Guardian; Action Images; Shutterstock; ReutersManchester UnitedAn unmanageable club? Carrick the latest to suffer in Manchester United’s faded grandeurOnly Matt Busby and Alex Ferguson have truly succeeded in the Old Trafford hot seat with each casting uneasy shadowsJohn BrewinTue 27 Oct 2026 16.02 EDTLast modified on Tue 27 Oct 2026 16.04 EDTSharePrefer the Guardian on GoogleShould any football club fit the Great Man theory of history it isManchester United. In the past 100 years, only Matt Busby and Alex Ferguson have knocked the club into shape. A pair of 20th-century Scotsmen, born 15 miles apart in Bellshill and Govan respectively, found the key. Otherwise, United has been a managerial dustbin, Michael Carrick the latest likely lobbed on the pile.Busby and Ferguson built the club around themselves, possessing the charisma to convince others that theirs was the path to follow. Carrick, an insider, a club man, is falling victim to the same isolation ashis predecessors in failure. Bruno Fernandes andLisandro Martínez going off-pistein TV interviews to depth charge Carrick were actually following club tradition. With glamour comes decadence, the faded grandeur that has so often chased a United manager out the door.Beyond Busby and Ferguson, each United manager who also served felt the lash of desperation of a falling giant. Each of their defenestrations has featured an infighting that would not have been out of place in ancient Rome. Favouritism, nepotism, self-interest, entitlement, complacency and sentimentality have been the betrayal of a legend, to use the title of Michael Crick’s and David Smith’s “j’accuse” book from 1989. Living with the legend and influence of those two managers leads the list of difficulties.United fans know such history too well. “You lousy bastards, you let him down,” Brian Kidd told teammates when the bullet came for Wilf McGuinness, Busby’s immediate successor, in December 1970. Busby himself had done the deed. A December 1972 meeting at Selhurst Park with Tommy Docherty as Crystal Palace beat United 5-0 hastened the end for Frank O’Farrell.View image in fullscreenAlex Ferguson shows off the team hat and scarf after his appointment as Manchester United manager in November 1986.Photograph: Gerry Crowther/Mirrorpix/Getty ImagesDocherty’s turn came. His sacking in 1977 after an affair with the physio’s wife was announced by the club secretary, Les Olive, from behind the oak door of the chairman Louis Edwards’ Cheshire mansion. Dave Sexton was sacked in 1981 despite winning his last seven matches. Falling attendances at “Cold Trafford” did for “Whispering Dave”. Ron Atkinson turned his November 1986 sacking into a party in the office that also housed the club sunbed. Big Ron’s parting gift was the hangovers that greeted Ferguson’s first day in charge.Ferguson’s predecessors had been intimidated by the fog of pipe smoke wafting down Old Trafford’s corridors. O’Farrell had needed to ask Busby if the former manager could vacate the manager’s office. “A fantasy world” is how O’Farrell described Busby’s coterie of gossipy former players who teed off with “the old man” at Davyhulme golf course. “There was no reality in the myth,” the Corkman dubbed “O’Failure” said in 1991.Busby’s indulgence of George Best, careering towards oblivion, created problems O’Farrell found unsolvable. Docherty showed the political wiles to jettison Best in January 1974 but also shelling Bobby Charlton, Denis Law and Paddy Crerand created enemies. Falling in love with Mary Brown, with whom Docherty remained for the rest of his life, was enough for a boardroom moral majority to rid themselves of their turbulent manager.Major honours won by Manchester United managersFerguson’s successors must deal with his continued presence, the face in the crowd photographers and TV directors seek. His patronage of Malcolm Glazer’s 2005 takeover is a dubious legacy dragging down those who have followed him. Ferguson mostly keeps his own counsel, a well-remunerated club ambassador untilSir Jim Ratcliffe cancelled a £2m annual stipend in 2024. There have been slips. “You should always start with your best players,” Ferguson told the mixed martial arts fighter Khabib Nurmagomedov in 2021when Ole Gunnar Solskjær had dropped Cristiano Ronaldo, loose talk escaping to social media.Ferguson’s part inRonaldo’s disastrous return to Old Traffordevidenced continuing back-channel influence, echoing Busby and Best. Carrick, during his press conference last Friday, mentioned his chats with his former boss.The omission of Fernandes for the Bournemouth game, left to sulk on the bench in club tracksuit, was classic Fergie politics.View image in fullscreenThe Sir Matt Busby statue alongside the Manchester United club crest at Old Trafford.Photograph: Conor Molloy/ProSports/ShutterstockA Ferguson facsimile is a fool’s errand. Carrick might have learned the lessons dished out to Solskjær, to whom he was assistant. After refusing to use Ferguson’s parking space and misty-eyed chat of “the boss”, nobody was buying the affable, gentle Norwegian cosplaying as a Glaswegian hard man.skip past newsletter promotionFree newsletter |Every weekdaySign up toFootball DailyKick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of footballEnter your emailSign upafter newsletter promotionNot that an injection of the alpha male has been much more use. Time has been kinder to theLouis van Gaaland José Mourinho regimes as subsequent failures pile up, but both failed to embrace the expectations of attacking football.Not that other club traditions were avoided. The subterfuge that brought in Mourinho was as dastardly as any of the post-Busby knifings. “People know him as a larger-than-life character,” the executive vice-chairman Ed Woodward said on Van Gaal’s 2014 appointment. “My wife had to find out when she was in the lift with Woodward’s family,” Van Gaal said of finding, in the haze of celebrating the 2016 FA Cup final victory, thathe was being replaced. His former Barcelona assistant had successfully lobbied Woodward. Attempts have been made by the Glazers’ operatives and, since December 2023, Ratcliffe’s Ineos, to corporatise and professionalise but United’s innate excess and anarchy keeps overtaking rationale.View image in fullscreenJosé Mourinho during his tenure as Manchester United manager, in November 2018.Photograph: Nigel Roddis/EPAUsing the means of a Netflix special, Mourinho has retrofitted his part in the story, he and Ferguson revealing together the facthe turned United down in 2013. The inference is that if Mourinho had arrived then all would have been roses. It is an unconvincing attempt at airbrushing both men’s reputations. Where does that leaveDavid Moyes, the immediate successorpainted as afterthought? In July 2013, Ferguson was celebrated as kingmaker, Moyes the rightful heir.Moyes’s reputation is another enhanced by failures that followed, including Mourinho’s grumpy, fractious tenure. When emerging reluctantly from his Lowry Hotel bolthole, the Portuguese reduced himself to mocking club history with “football heritage” rants. Such a scorched-earth policy was echoed by Ruben Amorim, whileErik ten Hag’s retention by Ineos in summer 2024was as confusing to Ten Hag as to everyone else.An unmanageable club? Busby and Ferguson showed it can be done, though the chance of another empire recedes the longer the vanity, plotting and self-interest that personify United continues. And for that, Busby and Ferguson deserve a share of the blame.Explore more on these topicsManchester UnitedAlex FergusonOle Gunnar SolskjaerJosé MourinhoLouis van GaalMichael CarrickfeaturesShareReuse this content

title: Police called to Florida soccer game after parents say three-year-old benched for being too good | Soccer | The Guardian
description: Police were called to remove the parents of a three-year-old player at a soccer game in Florida over the weekend
Author: Guardian sport
Headline: Police were called to remove the parents of a three-year-old player at a soccer game in Florida over the weekend
Content: The incident happened in Florida over the weekend.Photograph: David Madison/Getty ImagesView image in fullscreenThe incident happened in Florida over the weekend.Photograph: David Madison/Getty ImagesSoccerPolice called to Florida soccer game after parents say three-year-old benched for being too goodOrganizer says parents were causing disturbanceNo one arrested or made to leave game in FloridaGuardian sportTue 27 Oct 2026 08.07 EDTLast modified on Tue 27 Oct 2026 16.14 EDTSharePrefer the Guardian on GooglePolice were called after a dispute involving the parents of a three-year-old player at a soccer game inFloridaover the weekend.The boy’s parentscan be heard on police body camerassaying their son, Nevada, had been kicked out because he was too good at soccer and was embarrassing the other children. However, an organizer at the game said Nevada had pushed other children and his parents had become argumentative when their son was taken out of the game.In police body camera footage the organizer of the event, who works for i9 Sports, a youth sports group, can be heard saying Nevada’s parents had caused a disturbance.“The kid is good. He’s great. Really good,” the organizer says in the footage. “He’s very advanced compared to the other ones, so he’s scoring a lot of goals. But he’s pushing the kids ... So, I try to tell him, don’t push; we want to play without pushing, right?”In audio of the 911 call, the organizer says Nevada’s mother was being “really, really disruptive, following me around and calling me names in front of this whole bunch of people.”Nevada’s parentsposted a clip of their sonat the event in which he can be seen dribbling around older children with ease. The video has since gone viral. Nevada cannot be seen pushing any other children in the footage posted by his parents.Allow Instagram content?This article includes content provided byInstagram. We ask for your permission before anything is loaded, as they may be using cookies and other technologies. To view this content,click 'Allow and continue'.Allow and continue“They’re mad at my son because he actually plays soccer. They’re literally kicking him out of this place because he’s good at soccer,” his mother says in the body camera footage. “First, they said he’s not passing, but nobody’s catching the ball when he’s passing.”The i9 Sports worker told police they were willing to give Nevada’s parents a refund if they left.“I just want him out. Immediately,” the organizer told police. “Just give me their names so I can give them their refund.”The Winter Park Police Department said the family agreed to leave the event and no one was arrested.skip past newsletter promotionFree newsletter |Twice weeklySign up toSoccer DeskJonathan Wilson and Guardian journalists bring expert analysis and reporting on the biggest stories in soccer.Enter your emailSign upafter newsletter promotion“The family stated the game was over and they were leaving. The family was cooperative with the officers,” the department wrote in a statement on its website. “No one was arrested, trespassed, or forced to leave the park.”i9 Sports said it was reviewing the incident and had contacted Nevada’s family.“We are aware of concerns being shared regarding an incident at a local i9 Sports program, and we take them very seriously,” i9 Sports said in a statement. “The respectful treatment and well-being of every child and family matter deeply to us.”One officer appeared to want to see more of Nevada though. “I kind of want to see him play. I bet he’s good,” he can be heard saying to another officer on body camera.Explore more on these topicsFootballFloridaUS sportsnewsShareReuse this content

title: Ruthless Brewers close in on World Series sweep after crushing Rays 10-1 in Game 3 | World Series | The Guardian
description: Jackson Chourio and Brice Turang sparked Milwaukee’s eight-run fifth inning, and the Brewers routed the Tampa Bay Rays 10-1 on Monday night
Author: Guardian staff reporter
Headline: Jackson Chourio and Brice Turang sparked Milwaukee’s eight-run fifth inning, and the Brewers routed the Tampa Bay Rays 10-1 on Monday night
Content: The Brewers were in dominant form against the Rays on Monday.Photograph: Dirk Shadd/Tampa Bay Times/ZUMA Press Wire/ShutterstockView image in fullscreenThe Brewers were in dominant form against the Rays on Monday.Photograph: Dirk Shadd/Tampa Bay Times/ZUMA Press Wire/ShutterstockWorld SeriesRuthless Brewers close in on World Series sweep after crushing Rays 10-1 in Game 3Milwaukee one win from first World Series titleBrewers lead series 3-0 after resounding win in TampaAssociated PressMon 26 Oct 2026 23.22 EDTLast modified on Tue 27 Oct 2026 07.23 EDTSharePrefer the Guardian on GoogleJackson Chourio and Brice Turang sparked Milwaukee’s eight-run fifth inning, and the Brewers routed theTampa Bay Rays10-1 on Monday night to move within one victory of their first World Series title.“The guys play hard,” Milwaukee manager Pat Murphy said after the game. “They don’t give in. They make every pitch count, and that’s what it takes to win. That’s the same thing that Tampa did all year. That team is very, very capable. This is a best-of-seven series. It looks like we’re in the driver’s seat, but it’s baseball. Anything can happen.”Rookie left-hander Robert Gasser pitched one-hit ball and faced the minimum through six innings as Milwaukee rolled to a 3-0 lead in theWorld Series. Game 4 is Tuesday night at Tropicana Field, where many Brewers fans showed up Monday and cheered from behind the visitors’ dugout.“I assure you 100% that we want to give the best of each of us,” Rays third baseman Junior Caminero said after the game. “But they’re just playing better and things are going their way.”Gasser allowed a line-drive single to Yandy Díaz leading off the bottom of the first and then retired 14 straight before Victor Mesa Jr walked to start the Tampa Bay sixth. With the help of a caught stealing and a double play, Gasser became the first starter to face the minimum 18 batters through six innings of a World Series game since Arizona’s Curt Schilling in 2001 – and the first left-hander to do it since Sandy Koufax for the Los Angeles Dodgers in 1965.Quick GuideWorld Series 2026ShowScheduleBest-of-seven series. All times US Eastern Daylight Time (EDT).Fri 23 OctGame 1:Milwaukee 3, Tampa Bay 2Sat 24 OctGame 2:Milwaukee 5, Tampa Bay 4Mon 26 OctGame 3:Milwaukee 10, Tampa Bay 1Tue 27 OctGame 4: Milwaukee at Tampa Bay, 8pm (Fox)Wed 28 OctGame 5: Milwaukee at Tampa Bay, 8pm* (Fox)Fri 30 OctGame 6: Tampa Bay at Milwaukee, 8pm* (Fox)Sat 31 OctGame 7: Tampa Bay at Milwaukee, 8pm* (Fox)*-if necessaryHow to watchIn the US, all World Series games will air on Fox and Fox Deportes, with streaming available through Fox One. In the UK, the series will be carried by TNT Sports. In Australia, fans can watch on ESPN, with streaming available through Disney+ and Kayo Sports.Was this helpful?Thank you for your feedback.Chourio went 4-for-5, William Contreras was 3-for-5 and Milwaukee racked up 16 hits off “Fastball Freddy” Peralta and five relievers to win their eighth straight postseason game and fourth in a row on the road.Of the 43 previous major league teams to fall behind 3-0 in a best-of-seven postseason series, only the 2004 Boston Red Sox rallied to win four straight when they beat the New York Yankees in the American League Championship Series.Gasser became the first starter for Milwaukee to get an out in the sixth inning this postseason. He has allowed one run in 15 innings over three starts, all on the road.Peralta, the MVP of the ALCS against Cleveland, ran out of gas against the Brewers. He was charged with five runs and seven hits in four and two-thirds innings against his former team.After a pair of tense, down-to-the-final-pitch, one-run games in Milwaukee, the Brewers put this one out of reach in the fifth with a postseason-record seven straight hits with two outs.Chourio began the rally with a one-out single and then stole second with two outs. Christian Yelich walked, and Peralta exited after Contreras’ infield single loaded the bases.The inning appeared to end when Caminero fielded Contreras’ bouncer and threw to second base for a forceout. But the call at second was overturned after a replay review, and Cam Booser entered.Turang ripped a liner that shortstop Taylor Walls couldn’t short-hop. It bounced off his glove and rolled into shallow center, allowing two runs to score.Garrett Mitchell followed with an RBI single, Cooper Pratt grounded a two-run double down the left-field line and Sal Frelick lined a run-scoring double to make it 8-0.View image in fullscreenBrewers second baseman Brice Turang tags out the Rays’ Chandler Simpson during the first inning of Game 3 of the World Series on Monday night at Tropicana Field.Photograph: Carmen Mandato/Getty ImagesCole Sulser replaced Booser and allowed an RBI single to David Hamilton and an RBI double to Chourio, who became the second-youngest player with four hits and a stolen base in a World Series game behind Ty Cobb in 1908.Of the 25 previous teams who took a 3-0 lead in the World Series, 21 swept and four won in five games.Originally the Seattle Pilots for one season in 1969, the franchise moved to Milwaukee and was renamed the Brewers in 1970. Their only other trip to the World Series came as an AL team and ended with a loss to St Louis in Game 7 in 1982.Led by the 67-year-old Murphy, the Brewers need just one more win to finally end their championship drought.The Rays led the AL with 98 wins in the regular season, swept the Yankees in three games in the ALDS and beat the Guardians in six games in the ALCS.View image in fullscreenMilwaukee’s Sal Frelick celebrates after hitting an RBI double during the fifth inning of Game 3 of the World Series against Tampa Bay on Monday night.Photograph: Carmen Mandato/Getty ImagesBut they made uncharacteristic mistakes on the bases and defensively in the first two games, and completely unraveled at home.Tampa Bay also have never won a World Series in 29 seasons. The Rays lost to the Phillies in five games in 2008 and to the Dodgers in six games in 2020.Wearing their white Devil Rays uniforms, they were eager to play in front of their home fans at the quirky, cavernous Trop, which had its roof shredded by Hurricane Milton in October 2024 and needed major renovations.But their cowbell-ringing, towel-waving fans among a sellout crowd of 40,388 couldn’t lift them past the surging Brewers.The Brewers led the majors with 103 wins, beat the Padres in four games in the NLDS and swept the Dodgers in the NLCS. With a win in Game 4, they would become the first team to sweep an LCS and World Series since the 1976 Cincinnati Reds.Explore more on these topicsWorld SeriesMLBBaseballUS sportsMilwaukee BrewersTampa Bay RaysnewsShareReuse this content

title: Kane’s Ballon d’Or triumph a glorious riposte to celebrity fawning of ceremony | Ballon d'Or | The Guardian
description: The England captain spoke movingly on a night of deserving winners and unintentional hilarity in London
Author: Barney Ronay
Headline: The England captain spoke movingly on a night of deserving winners and unintentional hilarity in London
Content: 1:27Harry Kane ends England's 25-year wait for a Ballon d'Or winner – videoBallon d'OrKane’s Ballon d’Or triumph a glorious riposte to celebrity fawning of ceremonyBarney RonayThe England captain spoke movingly on a night of deserving winners and unintentional hilarity in LondonTue 27 Oct 2026 04.00 EDTLast modified on Tue 27 Oct 2026 14.20 EDTShareWell, there’s something new. Football: now available in new, genuinely heartwarming flavour.There was a lovely moment at London’s Palladium theatre on Monday, with the clock creeping towards 11pm at the end of a startlingly shrill and bloated evening of never‑ending awards and never-ending award‑related excitement.Harry Kane claims men’s Ballon d’Or to end England’s 25-year wait for winnerRead moreNot just for Harry Kane, who isnow the 2026 men’s Ballon d’Or winner, and in the process placed indelibly in that lineage of elite footballers. But also, frankly, for anyone watching, as Kane stood on stage gazing a little shyly at his golden orb, and kicked off his speech by thanking everyone, paying tribute to everyone, everywhere, then finally cracking into tears and a strangled croak as he thanked his parents for sacrifices made, his wife for always being there, and even, in slightly jarring vibe-shift from the warm honeyed tone, José Mourinho.11:25Harry Kane triumphs with historic Ballon d’Or win - The LatestEven Kane’s biggest advocates will rarely claim their man is one of a kind,sui generis, in the mode of the Ronaldo-Messi godhead. But Kane is exactly this in his own admirably humble way.Not just an exceptional footballer, the best, most deserving men’s player in the world this year, a European golden boot, scorer of 89 goals since August 2025,Bundesliga champion, World Cup semi-final captain, model of extreme professionalism and care. He’s also quite clearly the nicest man, if not just in football, then possibly the world.Or at least it felt like that as he walked off in that very dear and tender way, the centre of the world in that moment, but also just keen to get off the stage and let everyone get on with clearing up.It would be wrong to say Kane’s victory in the final vote of the night redeemed the grotesqueness of the ceremonies itself. There was a roomful of hugely deserving winners here. But Kane hits particularly hard.View image in fullscreenAlexia Putellas and Harry Kane pose with their trophies at the end of the 2026 Ballon d’Or awards ceremony in London.Photograph: Tolga Akmen/EPAAnd the Ballon d’Or is, let us be clear, a horrendous event, albeit a supremely popular horrendous event. There was the usual pomp around the ceremony, staged this year at a fancy theatre close to Oxford Circus.This isn’t sport. It’s celebrity culture, red‑carpet fawning, the worship of images and people, and fame. Football isn’t supposed to be cocooned this way, to send the message that there are barriers and ropes and special people. Yeah, well, good luck with that.The night kicked off with French Montana in spotless white tuxedo performing on an open-air double-decker bus. He definitely speaks, clearly, carried well, seemed enthusiastic. If it all goes south from here, the evidence suggests French Montana could, at the very least, get a job as a London tour bus operator.View image in fullscreenFrench Montana performs during Ballon d’Or award ceremony in London.Photograph: Rasid Necati Aslim/Anadolu/Getty ImagesBefore long Thierry Henry and Kate Scott glided on stage, half an hour late, to add a little deft and easy charm to a furious schedule of pots and prizes.And the awards came thick and fast. The Spain manager, Luis de la Fuente, was named coach of the year. “I hope in the future I will become in English better,” were his first words at the lectern, throwing his hat in the ring for a disastrous pension-padding six months at Manchester United two years from now.There was a lovely moment as Burna Boy came on to present the Socrates award for charitable works to Bukayo Saka. He was asked if there were footballers who had inspired his love for the game. At which point he looked at Thierry and said, “definitely, one of them’s standing right there”, and of course he said it in his Burna Boy voice, looking Thierry deep in the eyes so smooth and deep, just almost an impossibly sexy moment.The Ballon d’Or can be unintentionally hilarious at times such as these. There were just so, so many video tributes, so much excitingly portentous music. This is a stage where everyone happening at every moment is very clearly the most important thing ever to happen, superseded only by the next thing to happen on that stage, and then the thing after that.View image in fullscreenThe hosts of the ceremony: Kate Scott and Thierry Henry.Photograph: Matthew Childs/Action Images/ReutersThe degree of fawning is startling at first, but glazed by familiarity before long. At one point Cristiano Ronaldo appeared very briefly in a fact-cut big-screen montage and the crowd shrieked a song, clutched its hand to its fevered throat, collapsed into the aisles in sheer priapic excitement.skip past newsletter promotionFree newsletter |Every weekdaySign up toFootball DailyKick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of footballEnter your emailSign upafter newsletter promotionAlthough by the time the original Ronaldo emerged onstage at 10.44pm, there was a sense of the genuinely vertiginous company Kane was about to join. Ronaldo read out the name inside the envelope, and the hall collapsed into cheers and yells and roars as Kane appeared onstage.And yes the Ballon d’Or is a fundamentally silly thing on its own terms. It jars with the basic concept of team sport, promoting instead the opposite of sport, the opposite of team culture, the modern disease of fawning parasocial engagement with star names. In many ways the world would be a better place if the Ballon d’Or was simply abolished, as an example to all who pore over reels and clips and the imagined qualities of their celebrity paramours.But it is also fascinating, unignorable, and endlessly moreish. All the more so this time. Kane as the Ballon d’Or 2026 is a genuinely fine, uplifting, instructive moment in the spotlight.View image in fullscreenBukayo Saka delivers his speech after accepting the Sócrates award from Burna Boy.Photograph: Jeff Spicer/Uefa/Getty ImagesIt is always tempting to talk about the journey these players make. Everyone has a backstory. Most footballers come from adversity. Kane has this, in his own way, 16 years into a professional career which has names such as Leyton Orient, Millwall, Leicester and Norwich on the timelines. He was unexceptional as a junior, didn’t stand out as particularly skilful or big or outstanding in his numbers. He played as a holding midfielder for a bit while Spurs decided what to do with him.Kane worked relentlessly. He was Millwall young player of the year in 2012, fitting bookend to the Ballon. He made it because he simply refused to go away, to stop working, honed instead the deeper skills in his quiver, the purity of his shooting, the range of his passing long and short.And Kane is exceptional in other ways. Without ever peacocking around promoting his brand, without really trying he remains the most likable, authentic, role‑model‑ish modern-dayEnglandplayer. For a man who never talks big or acts big he has a happy knack of becoming the key player wherever he goes. Perhaps Kane has become cool now. He has always been likable, with that mild-mannered air of a kindly Victorian chimney sweep with a hamster in his waistcoat watch pocket. In the Bayern years, Kane has become leaner, more glossed and handsome, jawline, tan, iconic Vampire hairline.Mainly he expresses a common confusion about what talent really is. Talent isn’t simply moments. Talent is also application, focus, craft, the ability to work, to make others better.View image in fullscreenHarry Kane celebrates after scoring a penalty against Paris Saint-Germain in last season’s Champions League.Photograph: Christophe Ena/APAnd yet his elite career has also been oddly grudging. Somehow the idea has always been out there that Kane is undeserving of these accolades, despite his own mildness and humility, his obvious team qualities, his relentless delivery of goals, effort, leadership. It is a genuinely odd conclusion given the opposite is so manifestly true, that this is an entirely uplifting story of overachievement, of hard work and applied intelligence, as opposed to the kind of talent that just needs to be flame‑throwered in the right direction.It is undeniably true that Kane’s levels can drop dramatically when he can’t perform at his full physical capacity. There have been moments where it has been tempting to wonder if he’s gone far enough as England’s captain in the past few years, if his body and his talent deserve a little care.Well, that just shows how wrong you can be.Explore more on these topicsBallon d'OrHarry KaneEnglandBayern MunichTottenham HotspurcommentShareReuse this content

title: Golden State Valkyries one win from WNBA title after Game 5 win over Atlanta Dream | WNBA | The Guardian
description: Kiah Stokes had 13 points, eight rebounds and three blocked shots as the Golden State Valkyries moved within one win of a championship in their second season
Author: Guardian staff reporter
Headline: Kiah Stokes had 13 points, eight rebounds and three blocked shots as the Golden State Valkyries moved within one win of a championship in their second season
Content: Gabby Williams and Tiffany Hayes celebrate during Monday’s win over the Dream.Photograph: Ezra Shaw/Getty ImagesView image in fullscreenGabby Williams and Tiffany Hayes celebrate during Monday’s win over the Dream.Photograph: Ezra Shaw/Getty ImagesWNBAGolden State Valkyries one win from WNBA title after Game 5 win over Atlanta DreamWNBA finals Game 5: Dream 55-64 ValkyriesGolden State lead best-of-seven series 3-2Valkyries could win title in second WNBA seasonAssociated PressMon 26 Oct 2026 22.39 EDTLast modified on Mon 26 Oct 2026 23.47 EDTSharePrefer the Guardian on GoogleKiah Stokes kept swatting shots on the interior, while Veronica Burton disrupted the Dream with her own quick hands to alter shots.And that crazed, violet-clad “Ballhalla” home crowd roared at every chance – watching theGolden State Valkyriesmove one win away from a championship in their second season with a 64-55 victory against Atlanta in Game 5 of the WNBA finals on Monday night.The WNBA finals are a basketball wonderland – unless you’re part of the Maga machineRead moreStokes had 13 points, eight rebounds and three blocks, and Burton contributed a nearly identical stat line with 13 points, eight rebounds and four blocked shots as Golden State got defensive once more to shut down Angel Reese and the Dream.The Valkyries have leaned on Stokes’ steady presence and postseason experience during this remarkable run.Quick GuideWNBA finals 2026ShowScheduleBest-of-seven series. All times US Eastern Daylight Time (EDT).Sat 17 OctGame 1:Golden State 68, Atlanta 64Mon 19 OctGame 2:Atlanta 79, Golden State 65Wed 21 OctGame 3:Atlanta 97, Golden State 71Sat 24 OctGame 4:Golden State 67, Atlanta 62Mon 26 OctGame 5:Golden State 64, Atlanta 55Thu 29 OctGame 6: Golden State at Atlanta, 12.30pm (USA/CNBC)Sat 31 OctGame 7: Atlanta at Golden State, 8pm* (USA/CNBC)*-if necessaryHow to watchIn the US, the series will air on NBC, USA Network and CNBC, with all games streaming on Peacock. In the UK, it will be carried by Sky Sports. In Australia, fans can watch through WNBA League Pass, with selected coverage also available through ESPN.Was this helpful?Thank you for your feedback.“We’re not here without Kiah,” Burton said. “Every single day, every single game, from the beginning. Just her veteran experience as well. It’s more than just defense.”Angel Reese finished with seven points, 15 rebounds and five assists – a big difference from her two standout performances in the first two games of the series at Chase Center. Reese shook her head when whistled for the second of her three offensive fouls with 7:43 to play.“I still believe in our team, I still believe we can win this,” Reese said.Fans screamed and clapped thunder sticks following the final buzzer as Stokes spoke from the floor to chants of “MVP!”“We appreciate you,” a smiling Stokes said. “We got one more.”On a night leading scorer Gabby Williams struggled to find her shooting touch, Golden State found that “strength in numbers” mantra coach Natalie Nakase has praised all season long and everybody made an impact. Veronica Burton had 13 points, eight rebounds and her postseason-best four blocks – tying Diana Taurasi in 2009 for most by a guard in a finals game.On Saturday, Nakase had changed up her lineup fora 67-62 Game 4 winby inserting Tiffany Hayes and Kaila Charles into the starting five. She stayed with those two Monday night, and it worked again. Hayes, who played 10 seasons for Atlanta and came out of retirement two years ago, had 12 points – and Nakase has said she wants to win it all for the veteran guard.Williams began two for 11 and missed all four of her three-point tries, but she converted a three-point play with 9:08 remaining to put the Valkyries ahead 49-42 and finished with nine points on three-for-14 shooting and six rebounds.Atlanta will now try to stave off elimination at home Thursday in Game 6 and force a deciding Game 7 back here at Chase Center on Saturday. The Dream hurt themselves with 17 turnovers that led to 21 points for Golden State.“Nothing’s changed, we win two games we’re champions,” Dream coach Karl Smesko said.skip past newsletter promotionFree newsletter |Weekly for the 2026 WNBA seasonSign up toWNBA 30A limited run women’s basketball newsletter dedicated to the league’s historic 30th season.Enter your emailSign upafter newsletter promotionView image in fullscreenAtlanta’s Angel Reese shoots over Golden State’s Kayla Thornton during the second quarter of Game 5 of the WNBA finals on Monday night.Photograph: Thearon W Henderson/Getty ImagesStokes hit a key three-pointer with 2:46 to go in the third quarter and another with 7:21 left in the game, which ignited chants of “Ki-ah! Ki-ah!” from the rocking, rally-towel-waving sellout crowd at Chase Center.“It feels pretty special,” she said. “I always know what I brought to a team, I always understood my value but just to hear an arena full of 18,000 fans it just really makes me feel appreciated and loved.”Stokes has recorded three or more blocks in six straight games, tying her with Lisa Leslie in 2003 for the longest such streak in a singleWNBApostseason.The Valkyries used a dominant second half after they led 25-22 at the break, the lowest-scoring first-half combined score in WNBA finals history.Rhyne Howard’s three-point play with 4:59 left in the third pulled Atlanta within 34-31, but after that it was Stokes, Burton and the Valkyries coming up with all the crucial plays on both ends.View image in fullscreenActor Zendaya attends Game 5 of the WNBA finals between the Valkyries and Dream on Monday night at Chase Center in San Francisco.Photograph: Ezra Shaw/Getty Images“That’s just been our staple all season, we really rely on our defense,” Stokes said.Golden State owner Joe Lacob promised a championship within five years in a bold declaration when the expansion franchise was granted to the Bay Area three years ago, yet this season has exceeded even what he could have envisioned.Neither team could find a flow from three-point range in the first half as they combined to shoot five for 29 from deep – three of 16 by Golden State and two for 13 by Atlanta.Earlier Monday, the league announced Game 6 would be played at the 17,000-seat State Farm Arena in Atlanta starting at 12.30pm US Eastern Daylight Time on Thursday – a time when many fans on both coasts will be working.“I’d like to see it be a national holiday for all WNBA championship games so whatever somebody can do,” Smesko said. “I hope everybody gets to see it somehow and I know that for some people it’s not realistic, they have jobs and won’t be able to make it. So I’m disappointed for that but I’m really hopeful that as many people can see the game as possible.”Explore more on these topicsWNBAAtlanta DreamGolden State ValkyriesBasketballUS sportsWest CoastnewsShareReuse this content

title: Eagles’ nightmare season deepens as Cowboys hand Philadelphia fifth straight loss | NFL | The Guardian
description: Dak Prescott threw three touchdowns and Javonte Williams ran for 155 yards as Dallas beat Philadelphia 38-21 to extend the Eagles’ losing streak to five
Author: Guardian staff reporter
Headline: Dak Prescott threw three touchdowns and Javonte Williams ran for 155 yards as Dallas beat Philadelphia 38-21 to extend the Eagles’ losing streak to five
